title: The Guardian Legend

ines_header.note: Both figures check out against the file. 16 + 131072 = 131088, the size of the file, with nothing left over for CHR - and byte 5 asks for none. Unlike some dumps this header carries no anomaly that has been found so far; bytes 8-15 are all zero, so it is plain iNES rather than NES 2.0.

chr.evidence: iNES byte 5 is $00. By the iNES convention that means the cartridge has no CHR ROM and the board carries 8 KB of CHR RAM instead, which the file confirms by its size: header + PRG accounts for every one of the 131,088 bytes. NOT YET ESTABLISHED from the ROM: which code uploads the tiles. Per the playbook that is the whole graphics problem on a CHR RAM cartridge, and no uploader has been traced yet. The 8192 figure is the standard size for the board and is NOT derived from anything in this file.

mapper.name: UxROM
mapper.description: Mapper 2. A single write to any address in $8000-$FFFF loads the PRG bank register, which selects which 16 KB bank appears at $8000-$BFFF. The last bank - bank 7 here - is hard-wired at $C000-$FFFF and cannot be switched out, which is why the interrupt vectors and the switching code itself live there. There is no CHR banking, no scanline IRQ and no mapper-controlled mirroring: the board wires mirroring fixed, and iNES byte 6 bit 0 says vertical.

bus_conflicts.description: UxROM boards put the latch on the same bus as the ROM, so a write to $8000-$FFFF is ANDed with whatever the ROM already holds at that address unless the two agree. This ROM avoids that in the textbook way: it keeps a table of the eight bank values at $FFF2-$FFF9 and switches by reading a byte from the table and writing it straight back to the address it came from, so the written value and the ROM value are the same byte by construction.
bus_conflicts.evidence: $D79F-$D7A2 is LDA $FFF2,Y / STA $FFF2,Y, and $D70B-$D70E is the same pair. Seven more sites do it with a fixed address instead of an index - $D719/$D71C for bank 0, then $D726, $D733, $D740, $D74D, $D75A, $D767 for banks 1 to 6, each preceded by LDA #n / STA $04. A byte scan of the PRG for the three store opcodes based at $FFF2 (8D/9D/99) finds no other site.

mirroring.description: iNES byte 6 bit 0 is 1, which the specification reads as vertical mirroring. Mapper 2 has no mirroring control register, so unlike the MMC1 cartridges this toolchain came from, this cannot change at runtime and the header's bit is the whole answer. NOT CHECKED: whether the game ever relies on that arrangement in a way the ROM would show.

vectors.description: $DC75, $FEDE and $DCF3, all in bank 7 - which is the only place they could usefully be, since bank 7 is the one the CPU can always see. All three were disassembled and all three decode as the code their name implies: RESET is a textbook power-on sequence (SEI/CLD/LDX #$FF/TXS, then three PPUSTATUS polls, then a clear of $0000-$07FF), NMI saves A/X/Y and runs a vblank handler that does OAM DMA from page 2, and IRQ is a real handler rather than a bare RTI - it polls PPUSTATUS bit 6 and reloads DMC_FREQ. See the vectors region for the byte-level argument.

prg_banks.evidence: Opens with a 9-entry JMP table at $8000-$801A, then $FF fill. Nothing else in this bank has been traced.
Opens with a 5-entry JMP table at $8000-$800E. Nothing else in this bank has been traced.
Opens with a 12-entry JMP table at $8000-$8023. Nothing else in this bank has been traced.
Opens with a 10-entry JMP table at $8000-$801D. Nothing else in this bank has been traced.
Opens with a single JMP at $8000-$8002 and then falls into what decodes as code at $8003. The one-entry table is the odd one out among the eight banks and has not been explained.
Opens with a 20-entry JMP table at $8000-$803B, the largest of the switchable banks. Nothing else in this bank has been traced.
Opens with a 7-entry JMP table at $8000-$8014. Nothing else in this bank has been traced.

prg_banks.role: the fixed bank: vectors, bank switching, the far-call trampoline
prg_banks.evidence: UxROM wires the last bank to $C000-$FFFF permanently, and this is the last of the eight. Confirmed rather than assumed: the three interrupt vectors in this bank's own tail point at $DC75, $FEDE and $DCF3, and all three addresses decode as sensible handlers when this bank's bytes are placed at $C000. The seven fixed-address bank-switch routines at $D714-$D76E and the generic one at $D705 are also here, as they must be - code that switches the $8000 window cannot be running in the $8000 window. The boot-time bank check at $FF23-$FF43 selects each of the other seven banks in turn and confirms it answers with its own number, so the reset path itself asserts that this bank stays put while the others move.

open_threads: Every bank opens with a table of JMP instructions. Per the playbook that table IS the complete inventory of cross-bank entries, so resolving all of them and checking the count closes is the next structural step. Counted by scanning for consecutive $4C from $8000: 9, 5, 12, 10, 1, 20, 7 entries in banks 0-6, and 124 in bank 7 from $C000. The bank 7 figure is a raw count of consecutive $4C bytes and is NOT established as the table's real length - a run of JMPs can end by running into code that happens to start with one.

The far-call convention is at $D76F: it pops the return address, reads three inline bytes after the JSR (the first of which it stores in $04, the live-bank shadow), calls through, and restores the bank on the way back. Nothing has been resolved through it yet. Per the playbook a far call is the one reference no grep for an operand will ever surface, so this has to be done before any claim that a block is unreferenced.
$04 is the live-bank shadow byte: every one of the eight switch routines writes the bank number to it. Its readers have not been enumerated.

The boot-time bank check at $FF23-$FF43 is resolved and annotated, but the routine it calls on failure, $DED2, and the byte it stores at $0180 are not. Until those are read, what the seven failure codes at $FF3A mean is open.
CHR is RAM, so no tile exists in this file as a tile. No uploader has been found yet and no graphics region has been claimed.

The trailing $FF runs at the end of each bank (37, 48, 16, 40, 14, 13, 46 bytes in banks 0-6 and 14 bytes at $FFE4 in bank 7) look like fill but are not claimed as regions yet, because nothing has been checked about them beyond their byte value.
No RAM map exists yet. $04, $10-$13, $26, $2B, $30, $FC and $FE are already named by the code read so far and have nowhere to be written down.
